Pro-democracy advocates stage a rally outside the EDSA Shrine in Quezon City on Thursday, September 11, 2025, denouncing the alleged corruption in flood control projects and demand accountability from government officials.

The groups call for the immediate creation of an independent commission to investigate irregularities and demand that all elected officials—particularly those implicated in flood control controversies—release their Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth. The groups emphasized that the scandals not only involve the massive misuse of public funds but also worsen flooding problems faced by communities.

Members of led by Tindig Pilipinas, NAGKAISA! Labor Coalition, Kalipunan ng Kilusang Masa, and Simbahan at Komunidad Laban sa Katiwalian (SIKLAB) joined the rally. | via Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News

TRANSPARENCY IN TRAVEL EXPENSES — VP SARA VS. BBM

The Office of the Vice President of the Philippines (OVP) has set the bar for accountability by releasing a detailed breakdown of its 2025 travel budget and the numbers reveal transparency and restraint.

As of July 31, 2025, the OVP had a total allocation of ₱62.5 million for international and domestic travel. Out of this, only ₱20.68 million has been spent so far:

- International Travel: ₱7.47 million, mostly for security and OVP personnel.
- Domestic Travel: ₱13.2 million, covering ceremonial, executive, and program-related activities across the country.

Most notably, not a single peso or ZERO (0) FUND was used by the Vice President Inday Sara Duterte herself for personal travel. Every expense was directed toward staff and security support.

Compare this with the Office of the President (OP). Under the 2025 National Expenditure Program (NEP), Malacañang is asked for ₱1.054 billion in travel funds. This is indeed ₱94 million less than the ₱1.148 billion provided in the 2024 General Appropriations Act (GAA)—an 8% reduction. But despite the cut, the numbers remain staggering.

To put this in perspective, the President’s travel budget is nearly 17 times bigger than the entire OVP allocation.

While VP Sara has already accounted for every peso as of mid-year, the OP’s budget remains a broad allocation without any comparable breakdown for public scrutiny.

What is even more alarming is the silence from the House of Representatives (HOR), particularly the Office of the Speaker, Martin Romualdez. The HOR, which wields the “power of the purse,” has no publicly available report on its travel expenses.

If the Vice President can release detailed utilization reports, why can’t the OP and the House, especially its leadership, do the same?

Transparency is not just about saving money; it is about proving to the people that public funds are spent responsibly. 

The OVP has shown that this is possible by publishing actual spending data. The OP, on the other hand, continues to justify billion-peso appropriations with little explanation, while the HOR remains opaque altogether.

In the battle for accountability, VP Sara Duterte has taken the lead.

Editorial: Tio Moreno
PS || Given the current situation of our country, it is just necessary for public officials to publicize their expenses. I am just wondering why there is no publicly available report about the OP and HOR’s travel expenses. This editorial is written as a form of protest to the Marcos admin to be transparent because while mainstream media is so obsessed with VP Sara’s millions of travel expenses, they are silent about BBM’s “billions” of travel allocati

Source: https://t.co/PbVjLCn8PC
